record.question: The common-emitter transistor circuit has —
record.explanation: A common-emitter transistor amplifier is used for appreciable voltage/current gain. For the usual bypassed small-signal circuit, voltage gain is approximately −Rc/re, which can have large magnitude; it is not zero or negligible. Reference: https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/storage2/courses/117107095/lecturers/lecture_19/lecture19_page2.htm. Original printed source and ordered choices independently reviewed.
